newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine millers see growing wheat flour exports.
newsitem.headline: Argentine millers see growing wheat flour exports.

text.p: Argentine millers exported 158,000 tonnes of flour, measured by weight of wheat, from January to March and look set to set to export more in 1997 than last year, a milling official said Tuesday.
"This year, at least up to March, we saw the continuation of the tendency for exports to grow," Horacio Goyeneche, executive director of Argentina's Milling Federation, told Reuters in an interview.
But he added that measures Brazil took in April restricting access by importers to short-term credit might have slowed growth.

Brazil is Argentina's biggest flour customer, followed by Bolivia. Argentina's flour exports totaled 430,000 tonnes, measured in wheat, or 320,000 tonnes, measured by weight of flour, in 1996. Brazil imported 150,000 tonnes of flour, measured in flour, and Bolivia took 132,000 tonnes.
Millers exported 57,000 tonnes of flour in January, then 51,000 tonnes in February, and 50,000 tonnes in March, Goyeneche said.
"If this sort of figures continue then exports this year will beat 1996," he said.
Flour exports tend to peak in December, January and February, when Argentina's wheat harvest is at its height.
A big boost for Argentina's millers this season is the country's bumper, 15.8-million tonne 1996/97 wheat harvest, up from only 9.5 million tonnes the previous crop year.
Wheat exporters had sold 8.5-8.6 million tonnes of the crop by the end of April, with about 2.4 million tonnes marked for Brazil, according to market sources.
Argentine flour exports should also be helped by a drive by the government to introduce a new system of classifying wheat quality for the coming harvest, Goyeneche said.

Argentine wheat flour exports have risen from almost nothing before January 1995, when the Mercosur customs union was formed and ended many tariffs between Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay. Chile and Bolivia have since signed free-trade agreements with Mercosur.
Goyeneche said that his association was persisting in its efforts to form a Mercosur-wide millers' group.
"This will be useful as issues affecting the trade are increasingly international and not just limited to one country," he said.
